channel.title: KrakenD Security Advisories
channel.description: CVEs and security advisories that may affect KrakenD, with our assessment of each one: false positives, affected versions and fixes.

item.title: CVE-2026-128085: telemetry/opentelemetry: Attribute Value Length Limit Bypass via U+FFFD Characters
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.5 / EE 3.0.5, 2.13.15. The OpenTelemetry-Go SDK truncates attribute values longer than the configured AttributeValueLengthLimit, but its counting skips valid U+FFFD replacement characters. A value made of those characters is stored whole, whatever the limit, so attacker controlled attributes can grow the memory of each span beyond what the operator configured. This is an incomplete fix of an earlier truncation advisory, affecting the SDK from 1.33.0 up to 1.46.x. Fixed in 1.47.0. This vulnerability does not affect KrakenD in its default setup.

item.title: CVE-2026-128086: telemetry/opentelemetry: Memory Amplification via Dense W3C Baggage Properties
item.description: Severity: medium. Fixed in CE 3.0.5 / EE 3.0.5, 2.13.15. OpenTelemetry-Go parses the W3C baggage header by turning every property of every member into its own object up front, then copies and serializes them again. A header that stays within the size limits but packs thousands of properties makes each parse allocate around 95 times its own size, about 778 KB for an 8 KB header. A client repeating such requests puts the process under heavy allocation and garbage collection pressure, degrading its performance. Affects OpenTelemetry-Go from 1.0.0-RC1 up to 1.46.x. Fixed in 1.47.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-116591: klauspost/compress: zstd Decoder Panic via Crafted Two-Block Frame
item.description: Severity: high. Fixed in EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. The zstd decoder in klauspost/compress can panic on a crafted frame made of two blocks. An FSE normalized count of 32768 wraps to -32768 when stored as an int16, so the decoder keeps stale table state from the first block and indexes beyond the table while decoding the second, instead of returning an error. Both the DecodeAll and the streaming decoder paths are affected, so any application that decompresses untrusted zstd input can be crashed. Affects all versions before 1.20.2.

item.title: CVE-2026-33813: x/image/webp: Corrupt Image Panic via Oversized Canvas on 32-bit Platforms
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in EE 3.0.4. On 32-bit platforms, the WebP decoder in golang.org/x/image/webp accepted canvas sizes whose pixel count overflows an int32 and returned a corrupt image that panics when accessed. A remote attacker able to submit such an image to an application that decodes it could crash the process. The issue is fixed in golang.org/x/image v0.42.0. This does not affect KrakenD, which never decodes images received from clients or backends.

item.title: CVE-2026-46601: x/image/webp: Panic via VP8 Alpha Channel Size Mismatch
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in EE 3.0.4. The WebP decoder in golang.org/x/image/webp did not check that the dimensions of a VP8 chunk match the canvas size. When the image also contains an alpha channel chunk, the decoder builds an image with mismatched color and alpha data and panics when it accesses alpha data out of bounds. A remote attacker able to submit such an image to an application that decodes it could crash the process. The issue is fixed in golang.org/x/image v0.43.0. This does not affect KrakenD, which never decodes images received from clients or backends.

item.title: CVE-2026-46604: x/image/tiff: Panic via Out-of-Bounds Strip Offset
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in EE 3.0.4. The TIFF decoder in golang.org/x/image/tiff panics when it decodes an invalid image containing an out-of-bounds strip offset. A remote attacker able to submit such an image to an application that decodes it could crash the process. The issue is fixed in golang.org/x/image v0.43.0. This does not affect KrakenD, which never decodes TIFF images.

item.title: CVE-2026-97033: cmd/go: Build-Time Code Execution via sysroot, target and Language cgo Flags
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.4 / EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. Building a malicious package that uses cgo could execute arbitrary code at build time through compiler and linker flags allowed in #cgo directives. --sysroot relocates compiler subprograms and startup objects to an attacker-controlled directory, Clang’s -target can run helper tools from the working directory, -isysroot and -Wl,-syslibroot can pass a file that GNU ld treats as a linker script, and -x accepted arbitrary input languages. This is a build-time issue in the Go toolchain and does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-97034: cmd/go: Command Execution via GCC Spec Files in cgo Linker Search Directories
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.4 / EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. When building with GCC, a malicious package that uses cgo could run arbitrary commands at link time through untrusted GCC spec files. Linking with -fopenmp, -fopenacc or -fsanitize= makes GCC search for spec files in the -L and sysroot directories, and in some cases in the working directory, so a package could ship its own. This is a build-time issue in the Go toolchain and does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-97035: cmd/go: Code Execution and Arbitrary File Write via Clang -gen and GCC -gnat cgo Flags
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.4 / EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. The -g* wildcard in the cgo flag allowlists also matched Clang’s -gen-cdb-fragment-path and GCC’s -gnatO, which take a second argument. A malicious package could write files to arbitrary directories at build time and desynchronize flag parsing so that later arguments reached the linker as unvalidated inputs, leading to code execution. This is a build-time issue in the Go toolchain and does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-97036: cmd/go: Code Execution on macOS via -l to_library in cgo LDFLAGS
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.4 / EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. On macOS, a malicious package could pass -l to_library <path> in #cgo LDFLAGS. The Apple linker recombines both arguments into -lto_library, which loads an arbitrary LTO plugin library at link time and runs its code. This is a build-time issue in the Go toolchain and does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-97037: cmd/go: Linker Script Injection via Split -Wl Flags in cgo
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.4 / EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. Split -Wl, flags that consume a following argument, such as -Wl,-rpath or -Wl,--just-symbols, accepted a bare second argument that the compiler driver passes to the linker as an input file. Together with several macOS and symbol flags that GNU ld interprets as linker scripts when they name a regular file, a malicious package could run arbitrary code at link time. This is a build-time issue in the Go toolchain and does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-97038: cmd/go: Code Execution via Crafted .syso Files and cgo Linker Inputs
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.4 / EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. The go command passed .syso files, direct linker inputs in #cgo LDFLAGS and libraries in -L directories to the external linker without validating their format. A malicious package could disguise a GNU ld linker script as a library, embed linker options in Windows or macOS object files, or trigger LTO plugins, executing code or injecting flags at link time. This is a build-time issue in the Go toolchain and does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-97043: cmd/go: Code Execution via Escaped Quotes in //go:cgo_ldflag
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.4 / EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. The compiler and the go command parsed //go:cgo_ldflag directives by splitting on quote characters without handling backslash escapes. A malicious package could smuggle disallowed linker flags past validation and execute code at build time, or make the go command panic. This is a build-time issue in the Go toolchain and does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-97054: net/http: HTTP/1 Server Crash via MaxBytesReader Header Race
item.description: Severity: high. Fixed in EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. When a request body wrapped in http.MaxBytesReader exceeds its limit, Go’s HTTP/1 server marks the connection for closing by setting a Connection: close response header without any synchronization. If the handler reads the request body in one goroutine while another one writes the response headers, the two writes race on the same header map and the Go runtime aborts the whole process. An attacker who can send oversized bodies to an affected server can crash it, a remote denial of service.

item.title: CVE-2026-97039: cmd/go: Flag Sanitization Bypass via cgo pkg-config Directives
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.4 / EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. The allowlist for #cgo pkg-config: directives permitted options such as --with-path= and --personality=, and package arguments pointing to local .pc files. A malicious package could make pkg-config load its own .pc files and inject compiler and linker flags that the go command would otherwise reject. This is a build-time issue in the Go toolchain and does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-97040: cmd/link: cgo Directive Injection via .syso Files Disguised as Go Objects
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.4 / EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. The linker parsed a .syso file starting with a Go object header as a Go compiler object, so cgo metadata directives embedded in it, such as cgo_ldflag, reached the external linker without validation. A malicious package could use this to inject arbitrary linker flags at build time. This is a build-time issue in the Go toolchain and does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-97041: cmd/compile: Host Linker Flag Injection via //go:cgo Directives
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.4 / EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. The compiler and linker did not reject commas in //go:cgo_* symbol and dynamic linker directives. On ELF platforms, a malicious package could split the resulting -Wl, options into arbitrary host linker flags, and overwrite the external name of an exported symbol. This is a build-time issue in the Go toolchain and does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-97042: cmd/compile: Linker Flag Injection via cgo_import_dynamic and PE DLL Names
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.4 / EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. The compiler only validated the first character of library names in //go:cgo_import_dynamic directives, and on Windows the DLL names read from PE object files were passed to the linker without validation. A malicious package could reference arbitrary files on disk through path traversal or inject special linker arguments at build time. This is a build-time issue in the Go toolchain and does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: GHSA-gcjh-h69q-9w9g: cel-go: JSON-Skipped Struct Fields Exposed via NativeTypes and ParseStructTag
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.4 / EE 3.0.4, 2.13.14. GitHub published this advisory for cel-go without an assigned CVE identifier. When an application registers Go structs as CEL types with ext.NativeTypes and ext.ParseStructTag("json"), fields tagged json:"-" are not skipped. They become CEL fields literally named -, so a user-submitted expression such as dyn(obj)["-"] reads their value, and they also appear under the - key when the object is converted to JSON. NativeTypes also registers every nested struct reachable from the registered type, which can expose secrets in dependency types the developer never reviewed. The advisory lists 0.29.0 as the patched version, but the fix only shipped in cel-go v0.30.0.

item.title: BDSA-2026-33757: go-openapi/swag: Stack Overflow via Deeply Nested JSON
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. The JSON utilities in go-openapi/swag (swag/jsonutils) parse and serialize JSON recursively with no limit on nesting depth. A deeply nested JSON document can exhaust the goroutine stack, and Go treats a stack overflow as a fatal error that crashes the whole process. The upstream fix adds a nesting depth limit, first released in swag/jsonutils v0.27.3.

item.title: CVE-2017-3204: x/crypto/ssh: Missing Default Host Key Verification Enables Man-in-the-Middle
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Versions of Go’s golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package released before March 2017 did not verify the server host key by default. SSH clients built on the library accepted any host key unless the application registered a verification callback, which allowed a man-in-the-middle attacker to impersonate the server. The fix made a host key verification mechanism mandatory. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2018-17075: x/net/html: Parser Panic on Template Elements in Frameset Insertion Mode
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Versions of Go’s golang.org/x/net/html package released before July 2018 mishandled the “in frameset” insertion mode. Calling html.Parse on input such as <template><object>, <template><applet> or <template><marquee> caused a runtime panic, so an attacker who controls the parsed HTML could crash the process. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2018-17142: x/net/html: Parser Panic on Nested Templates Inside MathML
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Versions of Go’s golang.org/x/net/html package up to September 2018 mishandled <math><template><mo><template>, which caused a runtime panic in parseCurrentToken during an html.Parse call. An attacker who controls the parsed HTML could crash the process. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2018-17143: x/net/html: Parser Panic on isindex Inside a Template Table Body
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Versions of Go’s golang.org/x/net/html package up to September 2018 mishandled <template><tBody><isindex/action=0>, which caused a runtime panic in inBodyIM during an html.Parse call. An attacker who controls the parsed HTML could crash the process. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2018-17846: x/net/html: Parser Infinite Loop on Nested Select Inside a MathML Table
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Versions of Go’s golang.org/x/net/html package up to September 2018 mishandled <table><math><select><mi><select></table>. The inSelectIM and inSelectInTableIM insertion modes did not follow the HTML specification, so html.Parse entered an infinite loop. An attacker who controls the parsed HTML could exhaust CPU. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2018-17847: x/net/html: Parser Panic on Nested SVG Inside a Template
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Versions of Go’s golang.org/x/net/html package up to September 2018 mishandled <svg><template><desc><t><svg></template>, which caused an index out of range panic in (*nodeStack).pop during an html.Parse call. An attacker who controls the parsed HTML could crash the process. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2018-17848: x/net/html: Parser Panic on Formatting Element Inside a MathML Template
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Versions of Go’s golang.org/x/net/html package up to September 2018 mishandled <math><template><mn><b></template>, which caused an index out of range panic in (*insertionModeStack).pop during an html.Parse call. An attacker who controls the parsed HTML could crash the process. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-88031: MongoDB Go Driver: GridFS Chunk Deletion via Query Injection in File Identifier
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. The GridFS component of the MongoDB Go Driver can interpret a caller-supplied structured file identifier as a query condition instead of a literal identifier. An authenticated user who can influence the identifier passed by an affected application may cause all file chunks in a GridFS bucket to be removed, leaving the stored files unreadable. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: BDSA-2026-16933: x/image/tiff: Panic via Out-of-Bounds Strip Offset
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. The TIFF decoder in Go’s golang.org/x/image module panics when it decodes a crafted TIFF image with an out-of-bounds strip offset, so an attacker who can submit images for decoding could crash the process. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: BDSA-2026-17353: x/image: Unbounded Memory Allocation When Decoding a Crafted Image
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Image decoding code in Go’s golang.org/x/image module can be made to allocate an unbounded amount of memory by a crafted image, so an attacker who can submit images for decoding could exhaust the memory of the process. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: BDSA-2026-17354: x/image/vp8: Panic via Mismatched Chunk Dimensions
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. The VP8 decoder in Go’s golang.org/x/image module panics when it decodes a crafted image whose VP8 chunk dimensions do not match, so an attacker who can submit images for decoding could crash the process. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: BDSA-2026-36001: html/template: Incorrect Escaping of Regular Expressions in JavaScript Literals
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Go’s html/template escapes regular expressions inside JavaScript literals incorrectly, which can lead to cross-site scripting in pages rendered from affected templates. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: BDSA-2026-37952: x/text: Excessive Resource Consumption in Punycode Encoding of Long Invalid Hostnames
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. The punycode encoding code in Go’s golang.org/x/text module consumes excessive CPU and memory when it encodes a long, invalid hostname. An attacker who controls the hostname being encoded could degrade the performance of the process. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-107324: MongoDB Go Driver: Panic via Integer Overflow in BSON Value Length Handling
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. An integer overflow in how the MongoDB Go Driver handles BSON value lengths can cause a runtime panic when an application validates or accesses a malformed BSON document. An unauthenticated attacker who can supply BSON bytes to an affected application may crash the process, causing a denial of service. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-107325: MongoDB Go Driver: Out-of-Bounds Panic via Malformed BSON Array Length
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. The MongoDB Go Driver does not properly validate the length of a BSON array. Calling bson.RawArray.Validate or bsoncore.Array.Validate on a malformed four-byte array causes an out-of-bounds index and a runtime panic. An unauthenticated attacker who can supply raw BSON array data to an affected application may crash the process, causing a denial of service. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-81521: MongoDB Go Driver: Write Redirection via Unescaped Database Name in Client Bulk Write
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. The Client.BulkWrite operation of the MongoDB Go Driver accepts a caller-supplied database name containing a reserved separator character without escaping it before building the target namespace. An application that passes untrusted input as a database name could have the write directed at a database and collection other than the intended ones. This does not affect KrakenD.

item.title: CVE-2026-116587: auth/validator: Go JOSE CPU Exhaustion via Oversized RSA Keys in Embedded JWKs
item.description: Severity: high. Fixed in CE 3.0.3 / EE 3.0.3, 2.13.13. Go JOSE validates every RSA private key it parses from a JSON Web Key (JWK) by passing the attacker-supplied n, e, d, p and q values to crypto/rsa PrivateKey.Validate(). Since Go 1.24 that validation is cubic in the size of the modulus and primes, so a single JWK carrying huge primes burns an excessive amount of CPU. The JWK does not need to come from a key set: a jwk parameter embedded in the protected header of a JWS, which ParseSigned parses, is enough. Affects go-jose v4 up to 4.1.5 and all v3 versions. Fixed in go-jose 4.1.6.

item.title: CVE-2026-116585: auth/validator: Go JOSE Panic During CBC-HMAC Decryption of JWE Tokens
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.3 / EE 3.0.3, 2.13.13. Go JOSE does not validate the parameters of a JWE that uses the A128CBC-HS256, A192CBC-HS384 or A256CBC-HS512 content encryption algorithms, and indexes into an empty buffer while decrypting it. Any application that calls ParseEncrypted, ParseEncryptedJSON or ParseEncryptedCompact and decrypts untrusted ciphertexts with these algorithms panics. Affects go-jose v4 before 4.1.5 and all v3 versions.

item.title: CVE-2026-116586: auth/validator: Go JOSE Crash via Deeply Nested JSON in Token Parsing
item.description: Severity: medium. Fixed in CE 3.0.3 / EE 3.0.3, 2.13.13. Go JOSE parses the JSON of JWS and JWE objects with a recursive decoder that has no nesting limit. Parsing a deeply nested JSON structure can exhaust the goroutine stack, and Go treats a stack overflow as a fatal error that no recover can catch, so the whole process crashes rather than the single request. Affects go-jose v4 before 4.1.5 and all v3 versions. Fixed in go-jose 4.1.5.

item.title: CVE-2026-78661: x/net/html: Quadratic Complexity When Coalescing Text Nodes
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.3 / EE 3.0.3, 2.13.13. Go’s golang.org/x/net/html parser appends adjacent text to an existing text node with string concatenation, both in addText and when foster-parenting text inside tables. Each append copies the accumulated string, so HTML made of many short text runs separated by ignored end tags makes html.Parse take quadratic time and allocations. An attacker who controls the parsed HTML can exhaust CPU and memory.

item.title: CVE-2026-97045: x/net/html: Namespace Confusion When Rendering Raw Text in Foreign Content
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.3 / EE 3.0.3, 2.13.13. When rendering a parsed document, Go’s golang.org/x/net/html package decides whether the text children of an element are literal by walking its ancestors, but the walk stopped at the nearest foreign (SVG or MathML) ancestor once it found an HTML integration point. That integration point can itself sit under an element foster-parented into a foreign namespace, so re-parsing the rendered output resolves the subtree in a different namespace than the original. Applications that sanitize HTML and then render it can emit markup that browsers interpret differently.

item.title: CVE-2026-111943: crypto/x509: TLS Impersonation via Compromised eMudhra Intermediate CA Keys
item.description: Severity: critical. Fixed in CE 3.0.2 / EE 3.0.2, 2.13.12. eMudhra generated the private keys of eight of its intermediate CA certificates incorrectly, which makes the keys trivially recoverable. These intermediates chain to roots that most operating system and language trust stores include, such as emSign Root TLS CA - G3. Anyone holding the keys can issue a certificate for any hostname, or a client certificate, that validates as trusted. The intermediates were revoked for key compromise on October 18 and 19, 2026, and browsers block them, but Go does not check revocation, so a Go program keeps accepting these chains for as long as its trust store includes the roots. Go 1.26.10 adds a hardcoded denylist to crypto/x509: Certificate.Verify now rejects any chain that goes through one of the eight intermediates, regardless of the system trust store or the CA files you configure. KrakenD verifies certificate chains in two directions, and both are exposed: Gateway to services: TLS connections to HTTPS backends, JWK and identity provider URLs, and telemetry exporters. An attacker able to intercept that traffic can present a forged certificate and read or alter requests and responses, including credentials. Clients to gateway with mTLS: when you enable enable_mtls, KrakenD also trusts the system CA pool unless you set disable_system_ca_pool to true. An attacker can mint a client certificate under a compromised intermediate and authenticate against the gateway without intercepting any traffic. Upgrading changes behavior on purpose: once you run the fixed version, any service whose certificate chains through one of these intermediates fails verification with an x509 error. Those certificates are already revoked, so their owners must reissue them anyway. If you cannot upgrade right away, update the CA bundle of the operating system or image where KrakenD runs, and set disable_system_ca_pool to true with an explicit ca_certs list on mTLS deployments.

item.title: CVE-2026-100349: kin-openapi: Nil Pointer Panic in ValidateResponse on Headers Declared with Content
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in EE 3.0.2, 2.13.12. Before kin-openapi 0.146.0, openapi3filter.ValidateResponse passes a nil header schema to decodeValue when an OpenAPI document declares a response header with content instead of schema. The document passes validation, but every response validation for the affected operation panics, even when the response does not carry the header. Applications ingesting untrusted specifications expose this as a remote availability issue.

item.title: CVE-2026-100351: kin-openapi: ValidationHandler Security Requirement Bypass via Encoded Path Operation Confusion
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in EE 3.0.2, 2.13.12. In kin-openapi 0.144.0 to 0.146.x, openapi3filter.ValidationHandler selects the operation to validate from the decoded URL.Path, while a downstream gorilla/mux router configured with UseEncodedPath can dispatch a different operation from URL.RawPath. When a public exact route and a protected parameterized route overlap after decoding, a request with an encoded path separator is validated as public and dispatched to the protected handler without running the configured AuthenticationFunc. Fixed in kin-openapi 0.147.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-100352: kin-openapi: Panic via YAML NaN and Infinity Values in OpenAPI 3.1 Request Validation
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in EE 3.0.2, 2.13.12. Before kin-openapi 0.148.0, the OpenAPI 3.1 validation path passes YAML NaN and infinity values to santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema without applying the library’s finite number guards. An unauthenticated client sending an application/yaml body containing .nan, .inf, or -.inf to an operation with a numeric constraint makes the dependency dereference a nil big.Rat during ValidateRequest and panic.

item.title: CVE-2026-100353: kin-openapi: Nil Pointer Panic via Array Schemas Without Items in openapi3filter Decoders
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in EE 3.0.2, 2.13.12. Three openapi3filter decoder paths missed by the fix for GHSA-p6wj-qrr4-pgh5 lack a nil items guard for legal OpenAPI 3.1 array schemas. An unauthenticated client triggers a deterministic nil pointer panic through an array query parameter, a deepObject query parameter containing an array property, or a form-encoded body whose array property appears inside an allOf, anyOf, or oneOf subschema. Affects kin-openapi 0.136.0 to 0.148.x and is fixed in 0.149.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-100354: kin-openapi: Fatal Stack Overflow via Circular allOf, anyOf, or oneOf Schemas
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in EE 3.0.2, 2.13.12. Before kin-openapi 0.149.0, runtime request, response, and direct schema validation lack cycle detection when an allOf, anyOf, or oneOf chain refers back to an ancestor schema, even though loading and document validation accept the circular reference. A request or response reaching the affected schema causes unbounded recursion in Schema.VisitJSON or openapi3filter.decodeValue. The resulting stack overflow cannot be recovered and terminates the whole process.

item.title: CVE-2026-100347: kin-openapi: Panic in Legacy Router via Non-Canonical HTTP Method on a Static Path
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in EE 3.0.2, 2.13.12. Before kin-openapi 0.145.0, openapi3filter.ValidationHandler uses the legacy router, which passes an unsupported or non-canonical HTTP method for an existing static path to PathItem.GetOperation. The default branch of that function panics before authentication runs, so an unauthenticated client can repeatedly send methods such as PROPFIND or a lowercase get to abort connections and flood the logs with stack traces.

item.title: CVE-2026-100348: kin-openapi: Spec Loader Panic via Self-Referential additionalProperties Reference
item.description: Severity: medium. Fixed in EE 3.0.2, 2.13.12. Before kin-openapi 0.145.0, openapi3.Loader can dereference a nil schema value while resolving an additionalProperties JSON Reference that points to itself. Loading a crafted OpenAPI document through LoadFromData, LoadFromFile, or LoadFromURI reaches this code before document validation and panics the loading process. Ordinary recursive schemas are not affected.

item.title: CVE-2026-56857: os: Root.MkdirAll Follows Junctions Out of the Root on Windows
item.description: False positive: KrakenD is not affected. Dependency updated as a precaution in CE 3.0.1 / EE 3.0.1, 2.13.11. On Windows, os.Root.Mkdir and os.Root.MkdirAll could create a directory outside the root when the final path component was a junction pointing to a nonexistent location. Code that relies on os.Root to confine filesystem writes to a directory could therefore be made to create directories elsewhere on the system. The fix stops resolving junctions. This does not affect KrakenD.
